summary: Session 1: shipped `python -m ai_router.modules create | rename | delete | assign-sets` -- the module lifecycle ported from the extension's moduleAuthoring.ts, against the unchanged docs/modules.yaml contract, with running-session refusals, next-set numbering, all-or-nothing rollback, and every session-state.json mutation routed through the sanctioned writer.

reason.specifics: Session 2 wires the extension's five existing context-menu commands to the CLI this session shipped and deletes the TypeScript lifecycle it replaces. That is a same-surface continuation: the orchestrator that authored the Python contract knows which TypeScript call sites depend on which guarantee, and the exit codes, refusal messages and JSON shape the launchers must branch on. No provider switch is warranted; cross-provider independence is supplied by verification, which excludes the orchestrator's own provider.

residuals.description: `_existing_lifecycle_slug` matches an existing lifecycle set by basename suffix only, so creating module `api` would reuse `payment-api`'s `-api-plan` / `-api-decomposition` sets instead of minting its own. The correct identity test is that the name, minus its numeric prefix, equals `<slug>-<kind>` exactly.
residuals.rationale: Mirrors the TypeScript `findExistingLifecycleSetSlug` behaviour exactly, so it is inherited, not a regression this session introduced. The verifier graded it a non-blocking nit and the round returned VERIFIED. Fixing shipped code after a passing verification round would stale the verification stamp and owe another routed round for an edge case, which the loop-discipline rule against edge-case exhaustion (operator ruling, Set 086) exists to prevent.
residuals.owner_rationale: Session 2 already edits this surface when it points the New Module command at the CLI, so the fix rides along at no extra verification cost.
